subject: science
passage: White-crowned sparrows are common songbirds across much of North America, but males in different areas sing noticeably different versions of their song, much as people in different regions speak with different accents. Studies have shown that these dialects are learned rather than inherited. A young male listens to the adult males around him during his first months of life and later practices until his song matches theirs. Males raised without ever hearing adult birds develop a simpler, unusual song instead.
stem: According to the text, how does a young male white-crowned sparrow come to sing the dialect of its area?

choices.A: By hearing nearby adult males early in life and later copying them
choices.B: By inheriting the dialect that its own parents sang
choices.C: By singing with other young males until they all agree on one version
choices.D: By moving to an area where its parents' dialect is common

explanation.why: The text says the dialects "are learned rather than inherited": a young male "listens to the adult males around him during his first months of life and later practices until his song matches theirs." The correct choice restates this process.
explanation.A: Correct. The young male listens to nearby adults in his first months and practices until his song matches theirs.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says the dialects are learned "rather than inherited."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says young males learn from adult males, not from one another.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never says young birds move to find their parents' dialect.
